summary: SWEPT 32 NUMERIC LEVERS (SIG 16, TOK 16 -- enumerated from src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers and src/tok/levers.py::TOKLevers as every Lever whose default is an int or float and not a bool; the other 4 of the 36 declared levers are the str levers SIG.mode, SIG.space, TOK.mode, TOK.probation_by) x 4 values {nan, inf, -inf, 0} = 128 CELLS, each in a fresh subprocess, each set as the generated PREFIX_FIELD environment variable through a real spine.assemble.build(dict(os.environ)) and then driven as far as the package goes today: SIG through build -> encode -> encoder_parameters -> cadence_due -> warm_up (800 real optimizer steps, checking every encoder tensor for finiteness before and after); TOK through build_vocabulary -> tokenize(regularize=True) -> tokenize(deterministic). COUNTS PER OUTCOME OVER THE 128: REFUSED_BADLY 50, REFUSED_BY_NAME 26, UNREACHABLE_TODAY 18, ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE 16, ACCEPTED_HARMFUL 11, CRASHED 0. THE SHAPE OF IT IS A TYPE SPLIT, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. 21 of the 32 levers are int-typed, and Lever.coerce's `int(float(raw))` refuses nan on all 21 with the good LeverError naming the lever -- so not one of the 11 ACCEPTED_HARMFUL cells is on an int lever. All 11 are on the 11 float levers, where coerce hands nan/inf straight through to a package that has no isfinite check anywhere. THREE ARE CRITICAL AND ALL THREE ARE THE FAB_BALANCE=nan SHAPE EXACTLY: SIG_TEMP=nan, SIG_VAR_WEIGHT=inf and SIG_COV_WEIGHT=inf each leave EVERY encoder parameter non-finite after warm_up while WarmupReport returns verdict='budget' with separation=nan -- and in the SIG_TEMP case the refusal that would have caught it stands three lines up (`if temp <= 0.0`), false for NaN. Two more are high: SIG_D=0 gives every window a width-0 signature on both mode arms while the separation probe reads a perfect 1.0, and TOK_DROPOUT=inf silently makes bytes_per_token measure 1.0 instead of 4.0 -- the one estimator SIG's single window width and DATA's splice gate are computed from. THE 50 REFUSED_BADLY ARE ALMOST ALL ONE LINE: 42 of them are int-lever x {inf,-inf}, where int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is NOT in Lever.coerce's `except (TypeError, ValueError)` -- so a value the spine's own single reader was written to type-check escapes it as a bare OverflowError naming nothing. That is one edit in src/spine/lever.py covering every int lever in the tree. FOR THE CENTRAL-VS-PER-PACKAGE RULING: 15 of the 16 legitimate cells are the value 0 and six of those are sentinels spelled out in the lever's own help string (TOK.freeze_at '0 means never freeze', TOK.retok_every, TOK.mint_pmin, TOK.mint_novel, TOK.probation_uses, SIG.warmup); a central refusal of 0 would break all of them. NOT ONE lever in either package declares any meaning for a non-finite value, so a central rule refusing nan/+inf/-inf in spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce would wrongly refuse ZERO cells in this surface while closing 46 of the 50 bad refusals and all 11 harmful ones.

Measured at step 1: loss=nan, grads(sum_abs,finite)={'emb.weight':(nan,False), 'proj.weight':(nan,False),'proj.bias':(nan,False)}. findings.detail: Every guard in the package is `dropout > 0.0`, which +inf passes, and the draw is `stream.random() < dropout` -- always true at inf. So every available merge is skipped on every counting segmentation. Two things follow and neither is reported: (1) the seed build mints 82 tokens instead of 181 with 82 refusals (tok.build_refused=82) and the vocabulary lands at 338 instead of 437; (2) bytes_per_token is MEASURED at 1.0 instead of 4.0. That number is the package's single estimator and it leaves TOK: derive.signature_width_bytes(LM.ctx, bytes_per_token) is SIG's ONE window width for the whole run, and DATA's splice gate reads it too -- so a TOK_DROPOUT typo silently makes the signature window four times too narrow, which is the C4/C5 family the whole of sig/api.py is built to prevent, arriving from the tokenizer. A probability lever has no upper bound check anywhere (nothing refuses 1.5 either).

legitimate_specials:
SIG.dense_window=0 -- the dense arm is entered while windows_since_boundary is BELOW it, so 0 means 'no window is ever in the dense phase; the gate is stuck on the throttled arm'. Declared and PRINTED as an unreachable Gate arm with its own arithmetic in src/sig/api.py::cadence_due ("SIG_DENSE_WINDOW=0: ... no window count is below 0 ... SIG_TRAIN_EVERY=1 cannot be reached."). Verified: out/SIG_dense_window_0_pos.txt.
SIG.warmup=0 -- 'no pre-loop budget; the encoder is handed to the loop at its random initialisation, which is a real configuration'. Declared as a named unreachable arm of Gate sig.adaptive_stop in src/sig/api.py::warm_up. Verified: verdict='budget' steps=0 probes=0 curve=[].
SIG.warmup_min_frac=0.0 -- bottom of the declared 0..1 FRACTION interval: no floor, the stop is eligible from the earliest probe. Boundary is declared at src/sig/api.py::warm_up's `frac < 0.0` refusal, which admits exactly 0.0. WORTH THE RULING PHASE'S ATTENTION: the reason that refusal gives for rejecting a negative share ('no step count is below it, so the stop is eligible from the first probe onward -- the guard removed rather than lowered') is equally true at exactly 0.0, which is admitted.
SIG.warmup_plateau_eps=0.0 -- the strictest flatness test: only two exactly equal probes count as a plateau. Coherent reading of 'relative gain below which the curve is declared flat'; implied by the declaration rather than spelled out. Verified at SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=200: verdict='budget', stop never fires.
SIG.var_weight=0.0 -- the variance hinge off. Implied by the declaration ('Weight on the variance hinge'); its sibling cov_weight declares 0.0 as off in as many words. Verified: verdict='collapsing' at separation 0.0239 -- the collapse alarm still fires correctly, which is what makes this a legitimate arm rather than a silent one.
SIG.cov_weight=0.0 -- DECLARED off, and the shipped default: sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.cov_weight, 'OFF BY DEFAULT BECAUSE NOBODY HAS SWEPT IT, NOT BECAUSE IT WAS TRIED AND FAILED'.
SIG.prototype_frac=0.0 -- DECLARED off, and the shipped default: sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.prototype_frac, 'OFF BY DEFAULT FOR A STATED HAZARD, NOT BY NEGLECT' (the assembler's partition would train the encoder that produces the partition).
TOK.freeze_at=0 -- DECLARED sentinel IN THE HELP TEXT ITSELF: tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.freeze_at, '0 means never freeze', with a comment paragraph ('0 IS STILL A SENTINEL AND THE CENSUS ASKED FOR THAT TO END') explaining why choices= cannot express it and why the sentinel stands.
TOK.retok_every=0 -- DECLARED sentinel IN THE HELP TEXT: tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.retok_every, '0 leaves already-emitted ids alone forever'. It is also the arm carrying the project's largest recorded effect (2.175 b/B and 94% real words at 0, against 4.364 and 26% at 3000), so a refusal here would refuse the better configuration.
TOK.mint_pmin=0.0 -- DECLARED sentinel IN THE HELP TEXT: tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.mint_pmin, '0 mints on frequency alone'. Shipped default.
TOK.mint_novel=0.0 -- DECLARED sentinel IN THE HELP TEXT: tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.mint_novel, '0 reproduces plain most-frequent minting'. Shipped default.
TOK.probation_uses=0 -- DECLARED off: tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.probation_uses comment, 'THE DEFAULT 0 MEANS OFF, which is what every recorded run outside those arms used'. Shipped default.
TOK.dropout=0.0 -- the regularizer off; shipped default, and tok/levers.py::TOKLevers.dropout says 'the default is 0.0 so it has never run'. Verified: build and both tokenize calls identical to the unset baseline.
TOK.seed_vocab=0 -- target 0: no seed build runs, v0 stays 256, bytes_per_token is measured at 1.0 which is CORRECT for the byte segmentation that results. Coherent and correctly instrumented; implied by build_vocabulary's `target = min(int(tok.seed_vocab), vocab._cap())` rather than declared in the help text.
TOK.build_passes=0 -- no tally-and-mint pass runs; tok.build_pass is present-and-0 (the loop's arm was entered and seeded), which is the file's own convention for 'ran and did not fire'. Coherent; implied by `for _ in range(passes)` rather than declared.
TOK.min_pair=0 -- no frequency floor: every counted pair is a candidate. Coherent reading of 'How many times an adjacent pair must have been counted before it is a candidate at all'; the build here is identical to the default because the seed_vocab target binds first.
NOTE FOR THE RULING PHASE: 16 of 128 cells are legitimate and 15 of the 16 are the value 0 -- a central refusal of 0 in spine/lever.py would break 15 working mechanisms in these two packages alone, six of them spelled out in the lever's own help string. A central refusal of NON-FINITE values only (nan, +inf, -inf) would break NONE of them: no lever in either package declares any meaning for a non-finite value, and the one lever whose comment explicitly warns that values outside its unit label are legal (TOK.mint_novel, 'a reader who takes fraction 0..1 as a bound on legal values will be surprised by 2.0, which is legal') is talking about 2.0, not about inf.

Their non-finite behaviour is LATENT, not absent: the arithmetic each one lands in is named in the stub's own docstring (a _due modulo for grow_every, ln-free threshold comparisons for mint_pmin and probation_residual, an exponent for mint_novel), and each is a nan-comparison-is-False or modulo-by-zero the moment a body is written. Re-run this sweep against TOK after P4 (tok) lands.

What is not covered is the floor gate, the prototype arm and the sig.floor_skips / sig.prototype_pairs counters -- floor_kinds=0 is a latent ZeroDivisionError in the floor expression and floor_kinds at a non-finite value would make the skip test a False nan comparison.
